summary_md:
# Investering er et håndværk alle kan lære

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-09-22  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Danish Millionærklubben episode (EuroInvestor) with guests Jens Løstrup (investor and author) and Lars Svendsen (chief analyst, Svendsen & Tudborg). US indices are at record highs while Danish stocks lag. Both guests call Novo Nordisk's 8% drop after its capital markets day an overreaction: Svendsen is building a position, while Løstrup stays out and expects more selling pressure. Løstrup defends his large holdings in Jyske Bank, Torm and ISS, which Svendsen questions. DSV is under pressure from management turnover and a difficult integration.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 NOVO-B — Novo Nordisk | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Svendsen bought a starter position after the drop and will add at 230. Both guests call the capital markets day selloff an overreaction; P/E ~10-11.

#### Reasoning

Guest Lars Svendsen sees a P/E of 10-11 as a bargain unless earnings halve. The pipeline and a planned tenfold semaglutide output support volumes. He caps the position at ~4% and may double it at 230. Guest Løstrup also calls the drop an overreaction but owns none, dislikes the M&A talk and expects owners to keep selling. Main risks: competition (Lilly, Zealand, Gubra) and US price cuts.

#### Sell Triggers

- Trump price deal not offset by lower rebates
- Market share erosion faster than expected
- Value-destroying large acquisition

> *"Og hvis nu går ned, yderligere ned, og det er jo så 230, så køber jeg resten af min nye stampposition"*

---

### 🟠 DSV — DSV | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Svendsen says it starts to look interesting around 1100. Løstrup avoids it due to management departures and a weak integration.

#### Reasoning

Guest Svendsen is watching DSV near 1100 but flags a huge integration and a company that may have become too academic. Guest Løstrup sold in 2024 after the CEO was fired, owns none, and is cautious given senior departures and the pre-close call that sent shares down 5.6%.

#### Sell Triggers

- Further senior management departures
- Integration problems deepen
- Weak Q3 report on 21.10

> *"hernede omkring 1100, så begynder den at ligne noget"*

---

### 🟡 JYSK — Jyske Bank | **HOLD** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Løstrup holds a large position and calls it still undervalued (P/E ~13 on 2027). Rising rates lift interest income; mortgage lending is ~half of earnings.

#### Reasoning

Guest Løstrup bought at 262 in 2000-01. EPS rose from 20 to an expected 90+, helped by buybacks and the Handelsbanken merger. Costs are flat and rising rates boost Q4 and next year. He will trim only slightly for balance. Guest Svendsen disagrees: he sees banks as black boxes and does not see Jyske as undervalued.

#### Sell Triggers

- Rising unemployment causing credit losses
- Better alternatives with ~70% upside
- Portfolio concentration too high

> *"Jeg synes, at banken og aktien stadigvæk er undervurderet."*

---

### 🟡 TRMD-A — Torm | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Løstrup is very happy holding: too few ships, war-disrupted routes, strong quarterly earnings. Svendsen sold, seeing limited upside to 270-300.

#### Reasoning

Guest Løstrup keeps Torm: tanker supply is tight, oil demand is still rising slightly, and wars have lifted freight rates. He expects a strong Q3, and Hafnia's ~20% stake adds takeover optionality. Guest Svendsen sold to fund Capital Tankers, seeing only ~20% left to 270-300 unless ship prices rise 20%.

#### Sell Triggers

- Freight rates normalize
- Price reaches 270-300 with little upside left
- Hafnia merger fails and Oaktree dumps shares

> *"Det er en aktie, jeg ikke har kunnet holde mig fra"*

---

### 🟡 ISS — ISS | **HOLD** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Løstrup has a large position: flawless Q2, higher profit growth guided, ~600m German settlement added to buybacks, US growth potential.

#### Reasoning

Guest Løstrup praises CEO Kasper Fangel and expects strong buyback momentum for the rest of the year. The US, where ISS has under 1% share, is the key growth lever, and he has no plans to sell. Guest Svendsen is negative: a goodwill-heavy company financing buybacks with debt, and he prefers DSV.

#### Sell Triggers

- US turnaround fails
- Profit growth stalls
- Debt-funded buybacks become strained

> *"Jeg har ikke planer om at sælge ISS."*

---
